content.title: About
content.content: Glutinous rice flour is a finely milled product made from sticky (glutinous) rice, widely used in Asian cuisine for desserts, noodles, adhesives and dough. It has a soft, slightly sweet texture and becomes highly sticky when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Glutinous rice flour is produced from rice varieties high in amylopectin, the component responsible for stickiness.
In Japan it is called “mochiko” and is used to make traditional sweets called “mochi”.
In Thailand the flour is a key ingredient in “khanom khen”, a popular coconut‑milk and mango dessert.
Glutinous rice flour is often used in gluten‑free cooking as a substitute for wheat flour.
When stored properly it can retain its properties for up to a year.

items.title: Rich source of energy
items.content: It contains easily digestible carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike some alternative flours, glutinous rice flour contains virtually no fat.

items.title: Contains small amounts of B‑vitamins
items.content: These help support carbohydrate metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Ideal for diets with digestive issues because it lacks irritating fiber.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Rare but possible allergic reactions in rice‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Low protein and fiber
items.content: Not a complete protein source; long‑term exclusive use without supplementation may lead to deficiencies.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Glutinous rice flour is used to make mochi, noodle adhesives, dumpling wrappers, desserts, breading, and as a thickener for sauces. Mix with water or milk to a smooth batter, then steam or boil according to the recipe.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth.
